definitions.explanation: A large, fan-shaped edible mushroom (Grifola frondosa) with a rich flavor, widely used in Japanese cooking. Grows in clusters at the base of trees.

examples.japanese: {舞茸|まいたけ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{天|てん}ぷら→天ぷら：04948_tenpura⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧おいしい。
{舞茸|まいたけ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{使|つか}った→使う：00473_tsukau⟧⟦{炊|た}き{込|こ}みご{飯|はん}→炊き込みご飯：05883_takikomigohan⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{作|つく}った→作る：00481_tsukuru⟧。
examples.english: I made mixed rice with maitake mushrooms.

notes:
The name literally means "dancing mushroom" — {舞|まい} (dance) + {茸|たけ} (mushroom). According to folk etymology, people danced with joy when they found this prized mushroom in the wild.

COMMON DISHES:
- {舞茸|まいたけ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{天|てん}ぷら→天ぷら：04948_tenpura⟧: maitake tempura (a classic)
- {舞茸|まいたけ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{炊|た}き{込|こ}みご{飯|はん}→炊き込みご飯：05883_takikomigohan⟧: mixed rice with maitake
- {舞茸|まいたけ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{味噌汁|みそしる}→味噌汁：04954_misoshiru⟧: miso soup with maitake
- {舞茸|まいたけ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{炒|いた}め{物|もの}→炒め物：08537_itamemono⟧: stir-fried maitake

COOKING NOTE:
Maitake mushrooms are known for containing a protease enzyme that breaks down protein, which can prevent egg-based batters and gelatin from setting properly. Heating deactivates the enzyme.
